standard_prerequisites: Context span 3585-3605: a transcendence basis of K/k is an algebraically independent collection {x_i} such that K/k(x_i; i in I) is algebraic

Zorn's lemma applied to the collection of algebraically independent subsets of G containing A; the union of a totally ordered family stays algebraically independent because polynomials involve only finitely many variables
core_obligations: Existence: for A algebraically independent and G generating E/F, Zorn gives a maximal algebraically independent B with A subset B subset G, and maximality forces every element of G (hence all of E = F(G)) algebraic over F(B), so B is a transcendence basis

Equicardinality, infinite case: each alpha in B' is algebraic over F(B_alpha) for a finite B_alpha subset B; B* = union B_alpha equals B (else an element of B minus B* becomes algebraic over F(B*)), and |B| <= |B'| by the count of the union of finitely many finite sets over infinite B'

Equicardinality, finite case: exchange induction on m = |B'| <= n = |B|; the irreducible relation f(beta_1, alpha_1, ..., alpha_n) = 0 involves some y_i, the exchanged set B* = {beta_1, alpha_2, ..., alpha_n} is again a transcendence basis, and induction gives m = n
proof_roadmap: Run Zorn on algebraically independent subsets between A and G and prove maximality gives a transcendence basis
Handle the infinite case through finite dependences and the union count
Handle the finite case by the exchange induction using the irreducible polynomial f
